items.title: 4.3 Properties of Matrix Addition, Scalar Multiplication and Matrix Multiplication (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle pages mein hum ne matrices ko jama karna, number se zarb dena aur aapas mein zarb dena seekha. Ab dekhte hain ke yeh operations kin qaidon (properties) ko maante hain. Aap ne numbers ke qaide parhe hain, jaise \(2 + 3 = 3 + 2\); in mein se kaun se matrices par bhi chalte hain aur kaun se nahin, yahi is page ka asal sabaq hai.
Kitab kehti hai: agar \(A\), \(B\) aur \(C\) diye gaye jama ya product ke liye conformable hon (yani orders mel khate hon), aur \(c\) aur \(d\) scalars (aam numbers) hon, to yeh properties sach hain:

items: (i) Commutative property w.r.t. addition: \(A + B = B + A\)
(ii) Associative property w.r.t. addition: \((A + B) + C = A + (B + C)\)
(iii) Associative property of scalar multiplication: \((cd)A = c(dA)\)
(iv) Existence of additive identity: \(A + O = O + A = A\) (\(O\) is null matrix and \(A\) is a square matrix)
(v) Existence of multiplicative identity: \(IA = AI = A\) (\(I\) is unit/identity matrix)
(vi) Distributive property w.r.t. scalar multiplication: (a) \(c(A + B) = cA + cB\)  (b) \((c + d)A = cA + dA\)
(viii) Left distributive property: \(A(B + C) = AB + AC\)
(ix) Right distributive property: \((A + B)C = AC + BC\)

blocks.text: Har property ko aasan alfaaz mein samjhiye: (i) jama mein tarteeb se farq nahin parta. (ii) teen matrices jama karte waqt pehle kaun si do jama hon, farq nahin parta. (iii) do numbers se baari baari zarb dena ya un ke product se ek baar zarb dena ek hi baat hai. (iv) null matrix jama karne se matrix nahin badalti, jaise numbers mein 0. (v) identity matrix se zarb dene se matrix nahin badalti, jaise numbers mein 1. (vi) number bracket ke andar har matrix tak pohanchta hai, aur do numbers ka jama matrix par alag alag lag sakta hai. (vii) teen matrices ki zarb mein pehle kaun si do zarb hon, farq nahin parta, bas tarteeb wahi rahe. (viii) aur (ix) bracket kholne ke qaide hain, baayen se aur daayen se. (x) number ko kisi bhi matrix ke saath laga sakte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Zyada tar qaide wahi hain jo numbers ke hain, aur is ki wajah yeh hai ke addition aur scalar multiplication khana ba khana aam numbers par hi hote hain. Lekin numbers se do farq bohat aham hain:
1. Multiplication ke liye commutative property nahin hai: \(AB\) aur \(BA\) aksar alag hote hain (neeche Example 3).
2. Isi wajah se left aur right distributive properties (viii) aur (ix) alag alag likhi gayi hain: (viii) mein \(A\) baayen hi rehta hai aur (ix) mein \(C\) daayen hi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Property (iv) ke baare mein: kitab "\(A\) is a square matrix" likhti hai, lekin \(A + O = O + A = A\) har order ki matrix ke liye sach hai, bas \(O\) usi order ki null matrix ho. Property (v) mein \(I\) ka order sahi hona chahiye: order \(n\) ki square \(A\) ke liye \(I = I_{n}\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin. Choti matrices se (vii), (viii) aur (x) check karte hain: \(E = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\), \(F = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\), \(G = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\).
\[E(F + G) = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 5 & 7\end{bmatrix}\]
aur \(EF + EG = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 5\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 5 & 7\end{bmatrix}\). Dono barabar, yani (viii) yahan sach hai.
Phir \((EF)G = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\) aur \(E(FG) = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\): (vii) bhi sach.
Aur \(2(EF) = (2E)F = E(2F) = \begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\): (x).
Khud karke dekhiye: har product row guna column se nikaliye aur in jawabon se milaiye.
Ab kitab ka Example 3, jo dikhata hai ke multiplication mein tarteeb kyun aham hai. Is mein har entry ke liye teen products jama honge, is liye har row alag step mein karenge.

blocks.title: Example 3
steps:
Given: \(A\) aur \(B\), dono \(3 \times 3\).
To find: \(AB\) aur \(BA\).
Method: row guna column ka qaida (4.2.4). Dono square aur same order ki hain, is liye \(AB\) aur \(BA\) dono define hain aur dono \(3 \times 3\) hongi. Aakhir mein dono ka muqabla karenge.

Step 1: \(AB\) ki pehli row
\[c_{11} = (2)(1) + (0)(2) + (1)(1) = 3\]
\[c_{12} = (2)(-1) + (0)(3) + (1)(-2) = -4\]
\[c_{13} = (2)(0) + (0)(-1) + (1)(3) = 3\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 1 (\(2, 0, 1\)) ko \(B\) ke teeno columns se baari baari milaya. Har entry mein pehla number pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se zarb ho kar jama hua; zero wale products seedhe zero ho jate hain, is se hisaab chhota ho jata hai.

Step 2: \(AB\) ki doosri row
\[c_{21} = (1)(1) + (4)(2) + (2)(1) = 11\]
\[c_{22} = (1)(-1) + (4)(3) + (2)(-2) = 7\]
\[c_{23} = (1)(0) + (4)(-1) + (2)(3) = 2\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 2 (\(1, 4, 2\)) ko \(B\) ke teeno columns se baari baari milaya. Har entry mein pehla number pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se zarb ho kar jama hua; zero wale products seedhe zero ho jate hain, is se hisaab chhota ho jata hai.

Step 3: \(AB\) ki teesri row
\[c_{31} = (3)(1) + (0)(2) + (6)(1) = 9\]
\[c_{32} = (3)(-1) + (0)(3) + (6)(-2) = -15\]
\[c_{33} = (3)(0) + (0)(-1) + (6)(3) = 18\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 3 (\(3, 0, 6\)) ko \(B\) ke teeno columns se baari baari milaya. Har entry mein pehla number pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se zarb ho kar jama hua; zero wale products seedhe zero ho jate hain, is se hisaab chhota ho jata hai.

Step 5: \(BA\) ki pehli row
\[d_{11} = (1)(2) + (-1)(1) + (0)(3) = 1\]
\[d_{12} = (1)(0) + (-1)(4) + (0)(0) = -4\]
\[d_{13} = (1)(1) + (-1)(2) + (0)(6) = -1\]
Kyun: ab tarteeb ulti hai: \(B\) ki row 1 (\(1, -1, 0\)) ko \(A\) ke columns se milaya. Dekhiye, matrices wahi hain lekin ab row \(B\) se aur column \(A\) se aa raha hai; isi liye jawab badal jayega.

Step 6: \(BA\) ki doosri row
\[d_{21} = (2)(2) + (3)(1) + (-1)(3) = 4\]
\[d_{22} = (2)(0) + (3)(4) + (-1)(0) = 12\]
\[d_{23} = (2)(1) + (3)(2) + (-1)(6) = 2\]
Kyun: ab tarteeb ulti hai: \(B\) ki row 2 (\(2, 3, -1\)) ko \(A\) ke columns se milaya. Dekhiye, matrices wahi hain lekin ab row \(B\) se aur column \(A\) se aa raha hai; isi liye jawab badal jayega.

Step 7: \(BA\) ki teesri row
\[d_{31} = (1)(2) + (-2)(1) + (3)(3) = 9\]
\[d_{32} = (1)(0) + (-2)(4) + (3)(0) = -8\]
\[d_{33} = (1)(1) + (-2)(2) + (3)(6) = 15\]
Kyun: ab tarteeb ulti hai: \(B\) ki row 3 (\(1, -2, 3\)) ko \(A\) ke columns se milaya. Dekhiye, matrices wahi hain lekin ab row \(B\) se aur column \(A\) se aa raha hai; isi liye jawab badal jayega.

Step 9: Muqabla
(i) aur (ii) mein pehli hi entry alag hai (\(3 \ne 1\)), is liye \(AB \ne BA\).
Kyun: do matrices tabhi barabar hain jab har position ki entry barabar ho; ek entry ka farq kaafi hai.

Tasdeeq: diagonal entries ka jama (trace) \(AB\) aur \(BA\) ka hamesha barabar hota hai, ise ek tez check ke tor par istemal kar sakte hain: \(3 + 7 + 18 = 28\) aur \(1 + 12 + 15 = 28\). Barabar hai, is liye hisaab mein koi bari ghalti nahin lagti.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Aam tor par matrix multiplication commutative nahin hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: "Aam tor par" ke alfaaz aham hain: kuch joriyan commute karti hain (yani \(AB = BA\)). Misaal: \(AI = IA\), square \(A\) ke liye \(AO = OA = O\), aur \(A \cdot A^{2} = A^{2} \cdot A\). Lekin check kiye baghair kabhi \(AB = BA\) na maaniye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \((A + B)^{2} = A^{2} + 2AB + B^{2}\) har square matrices ke liye sach hai? Pehle khud sochiye.
Ishara: \((A + B)^{2} = (A + B)(A + B)\) ko properties (viii) aur (ix) se kholiye; \(AB\) aur \(BA\) dono aate hain. Kya woh hamesha jud kar \(2AB\) bante hain? Yeh sawal Exercise 4.1 mein aap ka intezar kar raha hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Addition commutative aur associative hai; \(O\) additive identity hai.
2. \(I\) multiplicative identity hai: \(IA = AI = A\).
3. Multiplication associative hai, \(A(BC) = (AB)C\), aur baayen aur daayen dono taraf se distributive.
4. Scalars kahin bhi aa ja sakte hain: \(c(AB) = (cA)B = A(cB)\).
5. Aam tor par multiplication commutative nahin: \(AB \ne BA\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(A(B + C) = BA + CA\) likh dena: \(A\) ko baayen hi rehna hai. Bachne ka tareeqa: bracket kholte waqt bahar wali matrix ki jagah mat badliye.
2. \(AB = BA\) maan lena, jaise \((A + B)^{2} = A^{2} + 2AB + B^{2}\) bina soche likh dena.
3. Orders mel na khate hon phir bhi property laga dena: har property is shart par hai ke jama aur products define hon.
